doc.title: Candido Camero — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Pay and weekend dances with Gloria Habanera
summary: The group worked Friday to Sunday, never recorded, and earned six pesos a week per person, about two dollars a dance, travelling across the republic.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: How long were you with the group Gloria Habanera?
Oh, many years, many years. I would say . . . from '35 to 1942. Yes.
No, never. Never. But we worked every weekend. Friday, Saturday and Sunday.
What did you earn per person?
Oh weekly. Well, for three days. Six pesos per person.
I guess that was a whole lot of money.

Well, back then it was more than a whole lot of money. (Laughs) More than a whole lot of money (Laughs). Yes, yes, two dollars per dance. Two dollars per dance. And the radio broadcast, 10 cents for the bus, so we wouldn't have to walk that far.
Maestro I imagine also that being as young as you were, you all were the great attraction of the girls.
Oh yes, yes. Across the republic, in all the republic. Every weekend traveling to different places in the republic always. Two dollars for each dance.
